## Practise a question type

Five compact tiles, one row: multiple choice **10**, short answer **4**,
calculations **1**, business report **1**, extended response **5** available.

- **Derived, not typed.** Every question of that canonical format in every
  sittable paper in the library. Parts count, parents do not, and both options
  of the either/or count.
- **The format is the contract's, not the section's.** 11(d), 12(c) and 13 sit
  in Section II, "Short answer", but are authored as extended responses. So
  Short answer offers 4 questions, not Section II's 8. A class told "do short
  answer practice today" gets 11(a), 11(b), 12(a) and 12(b). If the section is
  what a teacher means, that is a different entry, and it is not proposed here.
- **Outlined buttons.** The paper card's primary action stays the only filled
  button on the page.
- **A type session is its own attempt** (`docs/testmode-attempt-state.md`).
  Practising 11(a) here never marks it answered in the paper's sitting shown
  below it.
- **Not drawn, for review:**
  - a tile whose session is in progress would read *Resume practice* with its
    own answered count;
  - a type with nothing available would show *None available yet* and no
    action.

  Where Start practice goes, straight into the session or through a short setup
  on Page 3, is Page 3's to settle.

## What each part of the page is for

- **Header.** No paper is open, so the right-hand label is *Test mode* and no
  subject is named. The paper's subject appears in the header once it is opened
  (decision 4, and the P0 in decision 18). There is no Economics fallback,
  because there is no fallback at all.
- **Site navigation.** The app's own four tabs, in the shared tokens. Test Mode
  is a place on the website, not a separate application.
- **Page head.** One sentence covering both ways in, and the policy pill the shell
  already uses. **Import a paper** sits on the Practice papers heading: Test Mode
  owns exam import.
- **Paper card, three columns.**
  - Who the paper is: course and stage from the curriculum block, the title (a
    link to the overview), and questions, sections, marks and time from the
    contract.
  - Where the attempt stands: the status and its counts.
  - What to do next: one filled button, at most one outlined button, and
    **Delete paper** as an underlined text control beneath them. Delete is
    reachable and never the same weight as Resume. It turns coral on hover and
    asks for confirmation.

## Where each action goes

| action | goes to | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start paper | Page 3, overview | the instructions and sections are read before an attempt exists |
| Resume paper | straight to the saved item | the student has seen the overview; returning is one click |
| paper title | Page 3, overview | always, in every status |
| View results | Page 5, results (Slice B) | |
| Try again | Page 3, overview | a new attempt can choose different sections |
| Import a paper | Page 2 | |

## Decided here, open to change on review

- **Selected sections** appear as a line under the facts (*"Sections I and II
  only"*) only when the attempt is not the whole paper. None of the example
  attempts is partial, so it is described here and not drawn.
- **Not marked** joins the count line only when it is above zero.
- **Completed shows the mark, not a percentage or a band.** The mark is what the
  paper is out of.
- **Try again keeps the last result.** A paper being retried shows In progress.
  Whether its card should also show the last completed mark is left for review,
  and not drawn.

- `1.5 : 1` reads as a ratio.
